analysis.title: What Matters Today: Pushing Back our Rate Hike to December, Pension Rebal is Now Behind Us, ETF Inflow Towards the Mags and Cyber, French 2027 Budget Adjustment (1 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Goldman now expects the second Fed hike in December instead of October. August core PCE rose 0.25% on the month, somewhat below expectations, and the year-over-year rate is 3.01%, well below expectations.
Goldman sees core PCE growing 3.0% on a Q4/Q4 basis, below the median FOMC participant forecast of 3.4%. It sees a strong chance the FOMC ultimately concludes that additional hikes are unnecessary.
NY Fed President Williams said the September policy action means there is no need for urgency and time to gather more information. Goldman cites this as a reason an October hike is unlikely.

Q2 real GDP was revised up 0.7pp to +2.2% quarter-over-quarter annualized, mostly from consumption revised up 0.4pp to +3.8%. Goldman attributes the Q2 spending strength to larger-than-usual tax refunds and expects consumer spending growth to slow somewhat in 2026Q4.
The estimated $30bn pension rebalancing equity sale, one of the highest ever, pressured the market at the end of the sessions this week. Armbrust treats it as one headwind that is now gone.

Remaining equity headwinds are tomorrow's payrolls, the continued rise in 10y and 30y yields, and bad seasonality going into the midterm elections one month away. The S&P is about 2% from all-time highs and any relief in rates would trigger a rally.
Armbrust says the asymmetry to own equities has improved but headwinds remain. He is constructive on equities in October and bullish into November and December.
SPX is on track to outperform RTY for 7 straight weeks, the longest streak since 2018, while XLK has outperformed SPX for 6 straight weeks. Mega caps are providing much of the market's support.

MAGS has had 12 inflow days in the past 13 sessions, one of its longest stretches of recurring demand since launch. RSP is on track for 7 consecutive weekly declines, which would tie its longest stretch.
AI-driven demand for cybersecurity exposure has cybersecurity ETFs on track for one of their best months of inflows in Goldman's dataset, about +$950mm.
Fixed income ETF trading volumes have accelerated rapidly as the 10-year yield pushed through 5% this month.
France's 2027 budget is due today. PM Lecornu targets about €54bn of adjustment to bring the deficit to 5.0% in 2027 from 5.4% in 2026, versus about 6.5% absent new measures.

Rich Privo says the OAT/Bund spread near 120bp already reflects the problem. The government has no majority and this is the last budget before the presidential election, so the opposition response matters more than the budget text. Even a 5% deficit leaves debt rising and France needs a larger fiscal recalibration.

Privo sees the more interesting tail as a weaker EUR rather than wider OATs. A future domestically focused government could look harder at France's EU contribution, and a real confrontation with Brussels would have broad implications for the union.

On French equities, heavy client selling of domestics is rational because taxation is likely to stay part of the solution, particularly for regulated and utility-like businesses. With spreads near 120bp and positioning heavily skewed, it probably takes little good news to cause a squeeze.
Le Pen's alternative budget proposal is expected in the coming weeks, likely just before parliamentary debates start on October 13.

tension_points.bull_case: Pension rebalancing is behind the market, the S&P is about 2% from all-time highs, and any relief in rates would trigger an equity rally. Armbrust says the asymmetry to own equities has improved.
tension_points.bear_case: Payrolls tomorrow, the continued rise in 10y and 30y yields, and bad seasonality into the midterm elections remain headwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A continued move up in 10y and 30y yields, with payrolls tomorrow as the next test.

tension_points.bull_case: With spreads near 120bp and positioning heavily skewed against French domestics, it probably does not take much good news to squeeze.
tension_points.bear_case: Even a 5% deficit leaves debt rising, taxation will likely stay part of the solution, and a weaker EUR from a confrontation with Brussels is the more interesting tail.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The opposition response to the budget and Le Pen's alternative budget proposal, expected before parliamentary debates begin October 13.
